messages:
Maya Support: FYI getting multiple customer escalations in eu-west-1 — repeated 503s and timeouts for hosted inference. Started ~20m ago. Gateway: 'upstream returned 503'. Can infra/runtime triage?
Amir Eng-Infra: I see an alert storm from the hosted GPU pool. Pulling logs now. Symptoms look like container exits (exit code 137) and sudden GPU memory saturation on a subset of nodes.
Lila Eng-SRE: Grabbed dmesg and container logs from gpu-node-14. Kernel OOM lines: 
```
Mar 15 10:02:12 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 7812 (python) total-vm:4342112kB, anon-rss:4022300kB, file-rss:0kB
Mar 15 10:02:12 containerd[pid]: container "runtime-open-xxl" exited with code 137
```
Lila Eng-SRE: Confirmed multiple containers killed by OOM within the same 5m window.
Jun Eng-Runtime: We pushed v2026.03.15-rt-opt earlier tonight. That rollout changed the KV cache prefetch heuristics and added a larger prefetch buffer for long contexts. Could be leaking or double-counting buffers under batch aggregation.
deploy-bot: Deploy event: rollout v2026.03.15-rt-opt started by @jun at 1950011400, promoted to 100% at 1950012200.
Amir Eng-Infra: Correlation: the spike in OOMs coincides with the rollout completion window. Metric: average per-container GPU mem usage jumped from ~9.8GB to ~18.6GB for open-xxl variants on long-context traces.
Maya Support: Customers included one payload that had ~17k token prompt + max_tokens 1024 and batch_size 10. They reported initial latency spike then timeouts then 503s. They provided request id r-0a1b2c3d which maps to gpu-node-14.
Jun Eng-Runtime: Repro note from my local run: when sequence_len > 16k and batch_size >= 8, kv_cache allocation spikes ~2x. Heap shows a second allocation slab for prefetch buffers that shouldn't be live. Likely a reference counting bug in the prefetch path.
Kai Eng-ML: If prefetch doubles allocation then combined with quantized model memory we hit device limits quickly. This matches exit code 137.
Amir Eng-Infra: Short-term actions I can take now: 1) throttle max batch size on affected GPU pool, 2) pin traffic away from the image (rolling revert), 3) add immediate alert to restart containers that go >85% GPU mem for >30s. Which should we do first?
Jun Eng-Runtime: Do all three. Revert to v2026.03.10-rt-stable for hosted pools as primary mitigation. Also push a runtime patch to add strict per-request kv cache accounting to prevent double allocation (hotfix to follow).
Amir Eng-Infra: Initiating rollback -> rolling restart to v2026.03.10-rt-stable on hosted-eu-west-1 pool. Canary started.
Lila Eng-SRE: Adding temporary alert rule and a script to evict/bounce worker pods that exceed configured GPU mem threshold. Also enabling small file-backed swap on affected nodes to reduce hard OOMs while we stabilize.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01 - Upstream worker memory regression causing 503s. Priority P1.
Maya Support: Notifying affected customers: message template saying we have pinned to previous runtime, investigating root cause, ETA ~30m.
Amir Eng-Infra: Canary shows revert succeeded on 3 nodes, memory usage back to baseline. Rolling to remaining nodes. ETA for full shift ~8m.
Maya Support: Customer update: one customer tried again and reported immediate success after the revert :thumbsup: — reducing noise.
Jun Eng-Runtime: I captured a runtime heap diff and trace. Tentative root cause: prefetch buffer list not cleared when batch aggregation triggers kv_cache merge. Repro steps below. I will open a PR with a guarded free and unit test.
Jun Eng-Runtime: Repro steps (local):
```
# helper generates very long tokenized prompt (approx 17k tokens)
python tools/gen_long_prompt.py --tokens 17000 > long_prompt.txt
# run against runtime container image (use test cluster or local docker)
curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate \ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  -d '{"model":"open-xxl","input":"'"$(cat long_prompt.txt)"'","max_tokens":1024,"batch_size":10}' \ \
  -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null
```
Jun Eng-Runtime: Expected: triggers high mem and OOM on v2026.03.15-rt-opt, no OOM on v2026.03.10-rt-stable.
Lila Eng-SRE: Saved crash dump and heap snapshot to s3://redwood-debug/incident-1950013000/ for root-cause analysis.
Kai Eng-ML: Suggest adding a guard in the routing layer to detect long-context + large batch combos and route them to a safer variant for now (and set per-tenant max_tokens defaults).
Amir Eng-Infra: Implemented temporary route rule: any request with inferred context > 12k tokens will be routed to stable image. Also applied per-tenant max_tokens cap for non-enterprise accounts to 512.
Maya Support: Customers updated with the mitigation details. One asked for SLA credit; CS handling.
Jun Eng-Runtime: I'll cut a hotfix branch and run internal stress tests varying sequence length and batch sizes. Will aim to deploy a patched image by EOD after QA.
Amir Eng-Infra: Rolling revert finished. All OOM alerts subsided. Keeping the temporary alert and routing rule active until fix lands.
Maya Support: Closing loop with customers who confirmed recovery. Will keep thread open for root cause follow-up and postmortem.
Jun Eng-Runtime: Postmortem action items (tracking): 1) revert bugfix in prefetch or fix RC-counting + unit tests, 2) add chaos tests for long-context batch combos, 3) add telemetry on kv_cache live bytes to detect regressions earlier, 4) add per-tenant hard caps and smarter routing policies.
Lila Eng-SRE: Adding followup ticket INC-2026-0315-01-RCA and scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow.
Maya Support: Thx team. Updating incident doc and customer comms.
